habitat.naturalHabitat: Human and animal gastrointestinal tract; also found in soil and water
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora; opportunistic pathogen, especially in hospitalized or immunocompromised patients
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widely found in soil and water

culture.colonyMorphology: Large, mucoid, glistening colonies due to the thick capsule

identificationClues: Very mucoid, large colonies on culture due to a thick capsule
Indole negative — distinguishes it from E. coli

virulenceFactors: Large polysaccharide capsule — antiphagocytic, main virulence factor
Siderophores — iron acquisition, prominent in hypervirulent strains
clinicalImportance.transmission: Opportunistic — endogenous spread from GI flora; nosocomial transmission via contaminated hands or equipment
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Important cause of hospital-acquired infections; carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRE) is a major antimicrobial resistance concern
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Extremely mucoid colony morphology plus indole negativity distinguishes it from E. coli among lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rods

examFacts.importantTest: Mucoid colony morphology; indole test (negative, unlike E. coli)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Large capsule producing very mucoid colonies; non-motile, unlike most Enterobacterales

sources.name: CDC — Klebsiella pneumoniae in Healthcare Settings
